claim: The zebrafish model recapitulates components of Leigh Syndrome French Canadian Type (LSFC).
source: Here, we present and characterize a new genetic revertible animal model that recapitulates components of Leigh Syndrome French Canadian Type (LSFC), a mitochondrial disorder that includes diagnostic liver dysfunction.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing that the zebrafish model exhibits phenotypes similar to LSFC.

claim: LSFC is a mitochondrial disorder that includes diagnostic liver dysfunction.
source: Here, we present and characterize a new genetic revertible animal model that recapitulates components of Leigh Syndrome French Canadian Type (LSFC), a mitochondrial disorder that includes diagnostic liver dysfunction.
evidence: This is established knowledge about LSFC as a clinical entity.

claim: LSFC is caused by allelic variations in the LRPPRC gene.
source: LSFC is caused by allelic variations in the LRPPRC gene, involved in mitochondrial mRNA polyadenylation and translation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the genetic cause of LSFC.

claim: LRPPRC is involved in mitochondrial mRNA polyadenylation and translation.
source: LSFC is caused by allelic variations in the LRPPRC gene, involved in mitochondrial mRNA polyadenylation and translation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the function of LRPPRC.

claim: lrpprc zebrafish homozygous mutants displayed biochemical and mitochondrial phenotypes similar to clinical manifestations observed in patients.
source: lrpprc zebrafish homozygous mutants displayed biochemical and mitochondrial phenotypes similar to clinical manifestations observed in patients, including dysfunction in lipid homeostasis.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data comparing mutant phenotypes to patient manifestations.

claim: lrpprc zebrafish homozygous mutants displayed dysfunction in lipid homeostasis.
source: lrpprc zebrafish homozygous mutants displayed biochemical and mitochondrial phenotypes similar to clinical manifestations observed in patients, including dysfunction in lipid homeostasis.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data on lipid metabolism in the mutants.

claim: Phenotypes in the disease model were rescued using a liver-specific genetic model therapy.
source: We were able to rescue these phenotypes in the disease model using a liver-specific genetic model therapy, functionally demonstrating a previously under-recognized critical role for the liver in the pathophysiology of this disease.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing rescue of phenotypes with liver-specific Cre recombinase.

claim: The liver plays a critical role in the pathophysiology of LSFC.
source: We were able to rescue these phenotypes in the disease model using a liver-specific genetic model therapy, functionally demonstrating a previously under-recognized critical role for the liver in the pathophysiology of this disease.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that liver-specific rescue reverses disease phenotypes.

claim: The mitochondrion is a complex and essential organelle whose dysfunction is linked to diverse human pathologies and diseases.
source: The mitochondrion is a complex and essential organelle whose dysfunction is linked to a panoply of diverse human pathologies and diseases.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about mitochondria.

claim: Mitochondria have multiple roles in cellular and physiological homeostasis beyond energy production.
source: The understanding of the traditional role of mitochondria as the powerhouses of the cell has evolved as its multiple roles in cellular and physiological homeostasis have been functionally enumerated far beyond its commonly known role in energy production via the electron transport chain (ETC) (Spinelli and Haigis, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Spinelli and Haigis, 2018.

claim: Mitochondrial functions rely on coordinated cross-talk between the nuclear genome and mitochondrial genome.
source: All these functions rely on a coordinated cross-talk between the nuclear genome and its mitochondrial counterpart (Vafai and Mootha, 2012).

claim: LSFC is an autosomal recessive mitochondrial disease with onset in infancy.
source: Here we focus on Leigh Syndrome, French Canadian Type (LSFC), an autosomal recessive mitochondrial disease with onset in infancy that manifests with diagnostic liver dysfunction (Morin et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Morin et al., 1993.

claim: The most common allelic variant in LSFC is due to an A354V transition in exon 9 of the LRPPRC protein.
source: The most common allelic variant is due to an A354V transition in exon 9 of the leucine-rich pentatricopeptide repeat-containing motif (LRPPRC) protein (Mootha et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Mootha et al., 2003.

claim: Patients with mutations in the LRPPRC gene experience cytochrome c oxidase (COX) deficiency.
source: Patients with mutations in the LRPPRC gene experience a diverse array of clinical features centered around cytochrome c oxidase (COX) deficiency.
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about LSFC patients.

claim: LSFC clinical features can include early onset of hepatic micro vesicular steatosis and chronic lactic acidosis in neonates.
source: These can include early onset of hepatic micro vesicular steatosis and chronic lactic acidosis in neonates.
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about LSFC manifestations.

claim: Individuals born with LSFC have an average lifespan of less than 5 years of age.
source: Individuals born with LSFC have an average lifespan of less than 5 years of age with most succumbing to a series of extreme, acute metabolic crises.
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about LSFC prognosis.

claim: Most LSFC patients succumb to a series of extreme, acute metabolic crises.
source: Individuals born with LSFC have an average lifespan of less than 5 years of age with most succumbing to a series of extreme, acute metabolic crises.
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about LSFC disease course.

claim: LSFC patients that survive early life crises show hypotonia, language and mobility deficits and delays, and muscle weakness.
source: Patients that make it past the early life crises show a lessened disease state characterized by hypotonia, language and mobility deficits and delays, and muscle weakness (Morin et al., 1993; Debray et al., 2011).

claim: LRPPRC belongs to the pentatricopeptide repeat (PPR) containing motif family of proteins.
source: LRPPRC belongs to the pentatricopeptide repeat (PPR) containing motif family of proteins.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the protein family classification of LRPPRC.

claim: The human LRPPRC protein has 33 predicted PPR domains.
source: The LRPPRC protein in humans has been reported to have 33 predicted PPR domains and is promiscuous, preferentially binding to different mitochondrial RNAs (Spåhr et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Spåhr et al., 2016.

claim: LRPPRC is promiscuous, preferentially binding to different mitochondrial RNAs.
source: The LRPPRC protein in humans has been reported to have 33 predicted PPR domains and is promiscuous, preferentially binding to different mitochondrial RNAs (Spåhr et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Spåhr et al., 2016.

claim: LRPPRC plays a role in the regulation of both nuclear and mitochondrial RNA expression at the transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels.
source: LRPPRC plays role in the regulation of both nuclear and mitochondrial RNA expression at the transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels (Liu and McKeehan, 2002; Mili and Piñol-Roma, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Liu and McKeehan, 2002 and Mili and Piñol-Roma, 2003.

source: Loss of functional LRPPRC in human fibroblasts, C. elegans, and mice revealed decreased stability of mitochondrial mRNAs, defects in mitochondrial biogenesis, decreased complex 1 and cytochrome c oxidase activity, and dysregulated mitochondrial translation (Cuillerier et al., 2017; Gohil et al., 2010; Xu et al., 2012; Köhler et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cuillerier et al., 2017; Gohil et al., 2010; Xu et al., 2012; Köhler et al., 2015.

claim: Loss of functional LRPPRC revealed defects in mitochondrial biogenesis.
source: Loss of functional LRPPRC in human fibroblasts, C. elegans, and mice revealed decreased stability of mitochondrial mRNAs, defects in mitochondrial biogenesis, decreased complex 1 and cytochrome c oxidase activity, and dysregulated mitochondrial translation (Cuillerier et al., 2017; Gohil et al., 2010; Xu et al., 2012; Köhler et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cuillerier et al., 2017; Gohil et al., 2010; Xu et al., 2012; Köhler et al., 2015.

claim: Loss of functional LRPPRC revealed decreased complex 1 and cytochrome c oxidase activity.
source: Loss of functional LRPPRC in human fibroblasts, C. elegans, and mice revealed decreased stability of mitochondrial mRNAs, defects in mitochondrial biogenesis, decreased complex 1 and cytochrome c oxidase activity, and dysregulated mitochondrial translation (Cuillerier et al., 2017; Gohil et al., 2010; Xu et al., 2012; Köhler et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cuillerier et al., 2017; Gohil et al., 2010; Xu et al., 2012; Köhler et al., 2015.

claim: Loss of functional LRPPRC revealed dysregulated mitochondrial translation.
source: Loss of functional LRPPRC in human fibroblasts, C. elegans, and mice revealed decreased stability of mitochondrial mRNAs, defects in mitochondrial biogenesis, decreased complex 1 and cytochrome c oxidase activity, and dysregulated mitochondrial translation (Cuillerier et al., 2017; Gohil et al., 2010; Xu et al., 2012; Köhler et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cuillerier et al., 2017; Gohil et al., 2010; Xu et al., 2012; Köhler et al., 2015.

claim: The liver is the major metabolic factory of the organism.
source: Given that onset of LSFC is marked by the neurological and metabolic crisis (Morin et al., 1993) and the liver is the major metabolic factory of the organism, therefore, the role of liver impairment in LSFC represents a unique aspect of mitochondrial disease unseen in traditional Leigh syndrome.
evidence: This is established knowledge about liver function.

claim: The role of liver impairment in LSFC represents a unique aspect of mitochondrial disease unseen in traditional Leigh syndrome.
source: Given that onset of LSFC is marked by the neurological and metabolic crisis (Morin et al., 1993) and the liver is the major metabolic factory of the organism, therefore, the role of liver impairment in LSFC represents a unique aspect of mitochondrial disease unseen in traditional Leigh syndrome.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison between LSFC and traditional Leigh syndrome.

claim: Mice harboring liver-specific inactivation of Lrpprc mirrored clinical manifestations marked by mitochondrial hepatopathy, growth delay, and reduced fatty acid oxidation.
source: Mice harboring liver-specific inactivation of Lrpprc mirrored similar clinical manifestations marked by mitochondrial hepatopathy, growth delay, and reduced fatty acid oxidation compared to controls (Cuillerier et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cuillerier et al., 2017.

claim: A lipidomic profile study on LSFC patients highlighted a novel role of LRPPRC in peroxisomal lipid metabolism.
source: Recently, a lipidomic profile study on LSFC patients highlighted a novel role of this protein in the peroxisomal lipid metabolism (Ruiz et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ruiz et al., 2019.

claim: Current diagnosis of LSFC hinges on measuring lactate levels in the blood and brain, COX activity in patient fibroblasts, and sequencing of the LRPPRC gene for mutations.
source: The current diagnosis of LSFC hinges on measuring lactate levels in the blood and brain, COX activity in patient fibroblasts, and sequencing of the LRPPRC gene for mutations (Debray et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Debray et al., 2011.

claim: There is a lack of a cure or effective therapies for LSFC patients.
source: The lack of a cure or effective therapies for LSFC patients signifies that current clinicians must shift their focus to relieving and controlling symptoms.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the current state of LSFC treatment.

claim: Zebrafish have been employed as a powerful potential vertebrate model organism to study human mitochondrial disorders.
source: Zebrafish have been employed as a powerful potential vertebrate model organism to study human mitochondrial disorders (Broughton et al., 2001; Steele et al., 2014; Sabharwal et al., 2019a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Broughton et al., 2001; Steele et al., 2014; Sabharwal et al., 2019a.

claim: A compendium of approximately 1200 zebrafish transgenic lines was created using the gene-breaking transposon approach, of which 204 were clonally validated and molecularly characterized.
source: Previously, we have reported a compendium of approximately 1200 zebrafish transgenic lines created using the gene-breaking transposon approach out of which 204 were clonally validated and molecularly characterized (Ichino et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ichino et al., 2020.

claim: The GBT construct is incorporated into the intron of an endogenous gene via Tol2 transposase.
source: The GBT construct is incorporated into the intron of an endogenous gene via Tol2 transposase and uses a splice acceptor site to create a fusion protein between the native transcript and red fluorescent protein (mRFP) gene that contains a transcription termination site.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of the GBT construct.

claim: The GBT construct uses a splice acceptor site to create a fusion protein between the native transcript and red fluorescent protein (mRFP) gene.
source: The GBT construct is incorporated into the intron of an endogenous gene via Tol2 transposase and uses a splice acceptor site to create a fusion protein between the native transcript and red fluorescent protein (mRFP) gene that contains a transcription termination site.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of the GBT construct.

claim: GBT insertion results in the translation of a truncated endogenous gene product fused to mRFP.
source: When inserted intergenically, this results in the translation of a truncated endogenous gene product fused to mRFP.
evidence: This describes the outcome of GBT insertion.

claim: The GBT construct enables spatiotemporal tracking of the trapped gene's natural protein expression in real-time.
source: This enables spatiotemporal tracking of the trapped gene's natural protein expression in real-time.
evidence: This describes the utility of the GBT construct.

claim: The GBT insertion is reversible due to two loxP sites located near each terminal repeat that enables removal using Cre recombinase.
source: This insertion is reversible due to two loxP sites located near each terminal repeat that enables the removal of the GBT cassette using Cre recombinase.
evidence: This describes the reversibility feature of the GBT construct.

claim: The revertible nature of the GBT construct allows for tissue-specific or ubiquitous rescue of the mutated gene.
source: The revertible nature of this construct allows for the reversion of the mutant back to wild-type alleles to allow for tissue-specific or ubiquitous rescue of the mutated gene (Ichino et al., 2020; Clark et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ichino et al., 2020 and Clark et al., 2011.

claim: The previous work reported over thirty new potential models of human disease.
source: The previous work (Ichino et al., 2020) reported over thirty new potential new models of human disease; we report here the characterization and detailed investigation of one, the mitochondrial protein-encoding locus lrpprc.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ichino et al., 2020.

claim: This study describes the first revertible zebrafish mutant with a single disruptive insertion in the lrpprc gene to model LSFC.
source: We describe here the first revertible zebrafish mutant with a single disruptive insertion in the lrpprc gene to model LSFC.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the model presented in the manuscript.

claim: lrpprc homozygous mutants mimic hallmarks observed in patients such as early lethality, defective muscle development, and decreases in mitochondrial transcript levels.
source: lrpprc homozygous mutants mimic many hallmarks observed in patients such as early lethality, defective muscle development, and decreases in mitochondrial transcript levels.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: lrpprc homozygous mutants exhibited altered dietary lipid metabolism.
source: In addition, altered dietary lipid metabolism along with mitochondrial dysmorphology was also observed in these mutants.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: lrpprc homozygous mutants exhibited mitochondrial dysmorphology.
source: In addition, altered dietary lipid metabolism along with mitochondrial dysmorphology was also observed in these mutants.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The in vivo protein trap line GBT0235 contained a single RP2.1 integration event within intron 22 of the lrpprc gene on chromosome 13.
source: Molecular analyses revealed that the in vivo protein trap line GBT0235 contained a single RP2.1 integration event within intron 22 of the lrpprc gene on chromosome 13 (Figure 1A–B).
evidence: This is supported by molecular analysis data and shown in Figure 1.

claim: The RP2.1 GBT protein trap cassette created an in-frame fusion between the upstream endogenous exons and the start codon-deficient mRFP reporter sequence.
source: The RP2.1 GBT protein trap cassette overrode the transcriptional splicing machinery of the endogenous lrpprc gene, creating an in-frame fusion between the upstream endogenous exons and the start codon-deficient mRFP reporter sequence.
evidence: This describes the molecular outcome of the GBT insertion.

claim: The mRFP-fusion resulted in a translation product predicted to be truncated from 1461 amino acids to 817 amino acids.
source: This mRFP-fusion resulted in a translation product that was predicted to be truncated from 1461 amino acids to 817 amino acids (danRer11).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and prediction.

claim: Direct protein comparison between zebrafish and human Lrpprc predicted proteins revealed a complex set of putative PPR motifs with different levels of homology.
source: The direct protein comparison between zebrafish and human Lrpprc predicted proteins revealed a complex set of putative PPR motifs, many of which had different levels of homology (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is based on computational analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: PPR proteins contain tandem arrays of degenerate ~35-amino acids motifs that fold into a hairpin of antiparallel alpha-helices.
source: PPR proteins contain tandem arrays of degenerate ~35-amino acids motifs that fold into a hairpin of antiparallel alpha-helices (Barkan et al., 2012; Yin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Barkan et al., 2012 and Yin et al., 2013.

claim: PPR proteins bind to their target RNAs in a modular and base-specific fashion.
source: PPR proteins bind to their target RNAs in a modular and base-specific fashion (Barkan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Barkan et al., 2012.

claim: The 5th and 35th amino acids of each PPR motif determine the target nucleotide.
source: The 5th and 35th amino acids of each PPR motif determine the target nucleotide, and the ordering of the repeat motif elements in the respective PPR proteins can function as determinants to assign sequence binding specificity (Yin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Yin et al., 2013.

claim: RoseTTAFold was used to derive predicted models for human and zebrafish Lrpprc proteins.
source: As no traditional structures for these protein orthologs were available, we derived predicted models using the AI-based protein structure prediction tool, RoseTTAFold.
evidence: This describes the computational method used in the study.

claim: Many of the resulting derived PPR motifs in human LRPPRC were observed to be shorter than the canonical 35 amino acid PPR consensus motifs.
source: Interestingly, many of the resulting derived PPR motifs in human LRPPRC were observed to be shorter than the canonical 35 amino acid PPR consensus motifs (Figure 2).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: The human and zebrafish Lrpprc protein structures revealed that the signature PPR motif helix-turn-helix repeats were packed in a rigid conformation.
source: However, the human and zebrafish Lrpprc protein structures revealed that the signature PPR motif helix-turn-helix repeats were packed in a rigid conformation (Figure 2A–B).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 2A-B.

claim: 34 PPR motifs were identified in the human Lrpprc ortholog.
source: This analysis identified 34 and 31 PPR motifs in the human and zebrafish Lrpprc orthologs, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 2 supplements.

claim: 31 PPR motifs were identified in the zebrafish Lrpprc ortholog.
source: This analysis identified 34 and 31 PPR motifs in the human and zebrafish Lrpprc orthologs, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 2 supplements.

claim: Several mitochondrial-encoded genes were identified as targets using the FIMO motif search tool.
source: We identified several mitochondrial-encoded genes as targets using the FIMO motif search tool of the MEME Suite, and the top twenty hits with high confidence scores are listed in Supplementary file 1B and C, for humans and zebrafish, respectively.
evidence: This is based on computational analysis using FIMO.

claim: The C-terminus half of zebrafish Lrpprc protein, which was deleted in the zebrafish GBT mutant allele, consisted of multiple PPR motifs for RNA-binding.
source: In addition, the structure of zebrafish Lrpprc protein revealed that the C-terminus half, which was deleted in the zebrafish GBT mutant allele, consisted of multiple PPR motifs for RNA-binding (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 2C and supplement 2.

claim: Animals homozygous for the GBT0235 allele exhibit ubiquitous RFP expression throughout the body at 6 dpf with strong expression in the liver, gut, and muscles.
source: For instance, animals homozygous for the GBT0235 allele (hereafter lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235) exhibit ubiquitous RFP expression throughout the body at 6 dpf with strong expression in the liver, gut, and muscles (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on fluorescence imaging shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Endogenous lrpprc transcript levels were negligible in lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235 as compared to lrpprc+/+.
source: Endogenous lrpprc transcript levels were negligible in lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235 as compared to lrpprc+/+, indicating a nearly complete knockdown (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The reticular mitochondrial network was marked by GFP in Tg(MLS:EGFP) zebrafish.
source: Across these tissue systems, the reticular mitochondrial network was marked by the GFP (Tg(MLS:EGFP)), and the expression pattern of the Lrpprc was marked by mRFP in the mitochondria.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach for visualizing mitochondria.

claim: An overlap was observed between the GFP and Lrpprc-mRFP fusion protein in the caudal fin of zebrafish larvae.
source: Composite images revealed an overlap between the GFP and Lrpprc-mRFP fusion protein in the caudal fin of the zebrafish larvae (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is based on confocal microscopy shown in Figure 3C.

claim: An overlap was observed between the GFP and Lrpprc-mRFP fusion protein in the muscle region.
source: Nuclei of myocytes were marked by BFP whereas an overlap was observed between the GFP and Lrpprc-mRFP fusion protein in the muscle region (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is based on confocal microscopy shown in Figure 3D.

claim: lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235 mutants had a similar survival percentage to lrpprc+/+ and lrpprcGBT0235/+ through 6 dpf, followed by marked mortality leading to 100% lethality at 12 dpf.
source: lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235 mutants had a similar survival percentage to that of lrpprc+/+and lrpprcGBT0235/+ through 6 dpf, followed by marked mortality leading to 100% lethality at the end of the follow-up on 12 dpf (Figure 4A).

source: In contrast, the survival trend was similar between the heterozygous mutants and the wild-type animals.

claim: The mortality rate was strongly affected by the lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235 genotype.
source: The mortality rate was thus strongly affected by the lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235 genotype.

source: To assess the impaired function of the lrpprc gene, an investigation of the transcript levels of mitochondrial-encoded genes revealed a significant drop-off in their expression in the lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235 mutants as compared to lrpprc+/+ (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: mtDNA copy number was not observed to be significantly decreased in lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235 mutants as compared to wild-type.
source: To interpret if the decreased expression of mitochondrial transcripts was due to a decrease in mitochondrial number, we did mtDNA copy number analysis on lrpprc homozygous mutants. mtDNA copy number was not observed to be significantly decreased in lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235 mutants as compared to wild-type (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on qPCR data shown in Figure 4 supplement 1.

claim: These findings are consistent with data observed in previous studies that have shown a crucial role for lrpprc in mitochondrial mRNA stability.
source: These findings are consistent with data observed in the previous studies that have shown a crucial role for lrpprc in the mitochondrial mRNA stability (Gohil et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Gohil et al., 2010.

claim: Analysis of zebrafish lysate using GC/MS revealed increased levels of lactate in lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235 mutants.
source: Analysis of zebrafish lysate using gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (GC/MS) revealed increased levels of lactate in lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235 mutants (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is based on GC/MS data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Survivors of early life metabolic crises associated with LSFC have multisystemic involvement and often show skeletal muscle phenotypes including hypotonia, muscle weakness, and mobility defects.
source: Survivors of the early life metabolic crises associated with LSFC have multisystemic involvement and often show skeletal muscle phenotypes including hypotonia, muscle weakness, and mobility defects (Sasarman et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Sasarman et al., 2015.

claim: Four dpf lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235 larvae exemplified a decrease in integrated density and mean gray value when compared with lrpprc+/+ siblings.
source: Four dpf lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235 larvae exemplified (Figure 5A and B) a decrease in integrated density and mean gray value when compared with lrpprc+/+ siblings (Figure 5C-E) and indicated a deficiency in muscle development specific to lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235 larvae.

claim: The decrease in birefringence parameters indicated a deficiency in muscle development specific to lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235 larvae.
source: Four dpf lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235 larvae exemplified (Figure 5A and B) a decrease in integrated density and mean gray value when compared with lrpprc+/+ siblings (Figure 5C-E) and indicated a deficiency in muscle development specific to lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235 larvae.
evidence: This is inferred from the birefringence assay data.

claim: Assessment for the muscle phenotype in 4 dpf liver-rescued homozygous mutants displayed a similar decrease in integrated birefringence density as compared to homozygous mutants.
source: Assessment for the muscle phenotype in the 4 dpf liver-rescued homozygous mutants displayed a similar decrease in the parameters for muscle integrity such as integrated birefringence density as compared to homozygous mutants (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on birefringence assay data shown in Figure 5 supplement 1.

claim: Performing a blindfold analysis on representative images across both genotypes, no significant difference in the necrotic signal represented by acridine orange spots was noticed.

source: Gene set enrichment analysis predicted oxidative phosphorylation and glycerolipid metabolism pathways to be depleted in the lrpprcGBT0235/GBT0235 mutants (Supplementary file 2).
